title: An Efficient On-Chip Reference Search and Optimization Algorithms for Variation-Tolerant STT-MRAM Read
problem: Reducing reference search time for STT-MRAM read operations under process and environmental variations. Conventional sequential reference search with linearly increasing levels is slow.
motivation: STT-MRAM requires variation-tolerant reference optimization; extended search time degrades performance and margin maintenance under cell degradation.
method: Three novel algorithms: (1) DRRS (Dual Read Reference Search) determines optimal reference from two array reads via statistical analysis, (2) TRRS (Triple Read) addresses cross-array variation, (3) SRS (Simultaneous Reference Search) optimizes P/AP states concurrently. On-chip operation enables prompt re-optimization.
key_novelty: Using statistical characteristics of read data to determine optimal reference in minimal array operations eliminates sequential search bottleneck.
contributions: 85% reduction in reference search time vs conventional methods
2x accuracy improvement with TRRS for array-level variation
Rapid re-optimization enabling degradation recovery and preventive margin maintenance
limitations: Limited to STT-MRAM; applicability to other emerging memory technologies not discussed.
